belief: If the right people were in power, I would finally be safe.
origins: Elections are framed as life-or-death, and each side warns of catastrophe if the other wins. Fear and hope get attached to leaders, and our sense of safety rises and falls with the polls.
teaches: “Put not your trust in princes, in mortal man, who cannot save.” “Some trust in chariots and others in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.” “It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in man.” “The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; He directs it where He pleases.” Paul writes, “there is no authority except that which is from God,” and “do not be afraid, for I am your God.” Leaders matter, and it is good to vote and pray, but safety rests in the Lord, who rules over all rulers.
self_statements: If they win, we are doomed.
Only the right leader can protect me.
I will not be okay until they are in charge.
The other side will ruin everything.
errors: Believing I am either safe or in danger depending on who governs.
Assuming I know what leaders will do.
Feeling afraid and concluding that disaster is coming.
questions: What am I afraid of, specifically?
Have I felt this fear before in other elections? What happened?
What does Scripture say about trusting leaders?
Where does my real security come from?
How can I pray and act without putting my trust in leaders?
truth: My safety and hope are in God, who rules over all rulers. I can vote, pray, and engage thoughtfully without placing the weight of my security on any leader or party.
hw_truths: I will not trust in princes.
God directs the hearts of kings.
I trust in the name of the Lord.
My security does not depend on elections.
log: Each week, note one time you moved from fear of leaders to trust in God.
actions: Write what you fear will happen.
Write what happened after past elections.
Pray for those you support and those you do not.
Rest in the shelter of the Most High.
prayer: Lord, I have looked to leaders for safety. You are my refuge and fortress. Settle my heart, and help me vote, pray, and live without fear. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “I will not put my trust in princes. The Lord is my refuge.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “If the right people were in power, I would finally be safe.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
